inputs.root_cause: XLIFF's obligation register has 6 obligations across XLIFF-PARSE-001/MODEL-001/VALIDATE-001/INLINE-001/MODULE-001/TEXT-001 sharing identical rule_text about sc's isolated attribute, all status=missing with zero evidence -- the largest fully-unbuilt cluster found this tick after surveying xliff's 22 missing obligations. No isolated-attribute handling existed anywhere in the package.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-7508113EBF7E4457 and its 5 cross-capability duplicates (25A6AEE1EE8FA679, 2D08D42095E5EFD9, 452A66EC673B7518, 4CDD66101DC1EEB9, E8055B0103E9E5CD) -- all promoted missing->partial
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 8 new tests prove validate() now detects sc isolated-attribute/matching-ec inconsistencies at unit scope, per content type (source/target), matching the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec prose and schematron F5S/F5T patterns exactly.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed xliff.yaml's 22 missing obligations; found a 6-obligation cluster sharing identical rule_text about sc's isolated attribute, entirely unbuilt (all source_symbols/tests/evidence empty).

2. Read the pinned OASIS XLIFF 2.1 spec HTML directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xliff-001.bin, section 4.2.3.4 sc): 'The attribute isolated MUST be set to yes if and only if the <ec> element corresponding to this start marker is not in the same <unit>, and set to no otherwise.' Confirmed the unit-scope (not segment-scope) explicitly: 'sc / ec ... isolated spans can reach over segment (but not unit) boundaries.'

3. Extracted the exact formal rule from the pinned XLIFF 2.1 schematron (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xlf-002.bin, schemas/xliff_core_2.1.sch), patterns F5S (source) and F5T (target): isolated='yes' sc is an error if a matching ec (by startRef) exists anywhere in the same unit and same content type; F5.1S/F5.1T confirm 'no'/absent is the schema default and additionally check canCopy/canDelete/canReorder/canOverlap consistency -- deliberately excluded from this slice's scope, which targets only the isolated-attribute-consistency rule this obligation's own rule_text names.
4. Surveyed the existing model: InlineElement.attributes already round-trips 'isolated' generically (untyped dict), so no model change was needed -- only a new validator-side check.

5. Discovered a related, pre-existing limitation while designing the new check: the existing per-segment _validate_inline sc/ec pairing check (xliff.inline.ec.unpaired) does not scan across segment boundaries within a unit, so a genuinely valid cross-segment non-isolated pair (which the spec explicitly permits) would still trigger a false 'unpaired' diagnostic from that OLDER, separate check. Verified via grep that no existing test locks in this behavior for a cross-segment case. Decided, consistent with this session's established discipline (e.g. UBL's detection-only namespace-shadowing precedent), NOT to modify the older check -- instead built a genuinely new, additive, unit-scoped function, and documented the adjacent limitation honestly in code comments and evidence rather than silently fixing or ignoring it.

6. Added _isolated_diagnostics(unit, diagnostics) to validator.py: for each content type (source/target) separately, collects every sc with an id and every ec's startRef across ALL segments in the unit, then flags isolated='yes' sc with a same-unit-same-content-type match, and isolated!='yes' (covers 'no' and absent, the schema default) sc with NO same-unit-same-content-type match.
7. Wired one call per unit into validate(), right after the existing per-segment loop.

8. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: isolated=yes/no-match valid; isolated=yes/same-segment-match violation; isolated=no/same-segment-match valid; isolated-absent/no-match violation; isolated-absent/match valid; target-side isolated=yes/match violation -- all 6 cases correct on the first attempt. Additional probes for cross-segment whole-unit detection and source/target scoping independence also correct on the first attempt.
9. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (381 tests, zero new fixtures) against the new check to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 381 passed unchanged.
10. Wrote 8 formal tests, all passing on the first attempt.

11. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (389 passed, was 381, +8), and the full 6-format regression (3296 passed, was 3288, +8; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

12. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-3f75f94a779b2617, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/xliff/ -q -- 389 passed, was 381 passed (381 passed unchanged BEFORE writing new tests, confirming zero false positives)

.venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3296 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3288 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule; every claim grounded directly in the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec HTML and pinned schematron source.
